action_summary: The machine remembered the answer and still paid full price to recognise the question. A fingerprint is taken by ACTING -- six probes, every action running a real program -- and it costs 5-8 s; discover took it twice per call and again on every repeat, so a one-action plan recalled in 4,757 ms against 4,766 ms cold. Failures were not remembered at all: the identical goal that needs 64,637 ms to fail spent 63,874 ms failing again on the next call. Now the fingerprint is cached under a key that names exactly what it is a fact about (this program list, each program's bytes on disk, this seed) and dies when any of them changes, and a refusal is remembered against the hash of the verifier that made it. Measured: gz 7,569 -> 265 -> 218 ms; png->jpg 16,669 -> 195 ms; dump->csv 63,473 -> 187 ms; hash 1,047 -> 238 ms. 'Learn it once' now buys speed on the second attempt, which is the only sense in which it is learning.
